title: Accept offline operations durably and distinguish queued work from authoritative results

requirements.section: 3. Local acceptance is not server commitment
requirements.invariant: A locally accepted operation is reported as durably queued and is never represented as authoritatively applied until a server result is observed.
The same operation identifier and payload replay to the same result, while reuse of that identifier with a different payload fails with a stable non-retryable mismatch.

Every durable command carries one stable operation ID, contract version, Account scope, actor intent, client evidence time, typed payload, and typed preconditions without provider values or dynamic persistence fields.

Only the reviewed draft, queued, applying, applied, rejected, superseded, and resolved transitions are legal; transient failures requeue and permanent domain or authorization failures reject without blocking unrelated work.
Callers observe one operation or the unresolved operations for one Account through a provider-free query port using stable snapshots and safe errors.

Connectivity, authentication freshness, required subscription readiness, checkpoint age, pending work, rejected work, transient failure, maintenance, migration, and required-update state remain explicit; online and synchronized are never synonyms.
Restart, transient retry, permanent rejection, lost response, duplicate delivery, retired contract, and account-isolation fixtures produce durable deterministic outcomes and stable diagnostics.

items: OperationID, AccountID, PrincipalID, OperationContractVersion, OperationEnvelope, and closed OperationPrecondition values contain only Ledger and standard Swift types.
OperationReceipt reports local queued acceptance; OperationSnapshot and OperationOutcome represent later authoritative or recovery state without provider SDK types.
OperationLifecycle validates the exact transition graph and classifies transient transport failure separately from permanent rejection.
ApplicationErrorCode, ApplicationErrorCategory, RetryDisposition, OperationRejection, and safe diagnostic summaries never expose raw vendor errors.
OperationFingerprint is deterministic for a canonical encoded envelope and detects same-ID/different-payload misuse.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This shared-contract slice introduces no Postgres relation; operation tables and result journals belong to provider-specific command-handler slices.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No business command is handled here; later slices must implement these lifecycle semantics in authoritative transactions.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Data API schema or relation is exposed.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: No server row or function is introduced; Account authorization remains a later RLS and handler obligation.

syncStreams.notApplicable: This slice defines portable operation/readiness values only; PowerSync stream definitions and unauthorized-local-row tests remain provider-specific slices.

items: The reference operation journal accepts an envelope once, returns the same receipt for exact replay, rejects payload mismatch, and persists as a Codable snapshot suitable for restart fixtures.
Unresolved operation queries are Account-scoped and cannot return another Account's queued, applying, rejected, or recovery evidence.
Restart preserves queued, applying, and rejected state; applying may be safely retried, and unrelated later operations are not starved by a permanent rejection.
SyncHealthSnapshot validates nonnegative counts and explicit oldest-pending timestamps and calculates online and synchronized state independently.

storageMedia.notApplicable: Attachment bytes and media queue durability are owned by the attachment lifecycle slice.

appMcp.notApplicable: This slice publishes the provider-free Swift contract and reference behavior; concrete app presenters, generated TypeScript contracts, and MCP endpoints are later entry-point slices.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase record is read and no target data is migrated by the shared lifecycle contract.

items: Safe operation diagnostics include stable error category, code, retry disposition, operation ID, and Account ID only; provider messages, payload bodies, credentials, and private text are excluded.
Sync health exposes pending/rejected counts, oldest ages, readiness, checkpoint, transient failure, maintenance, migration, and required-update state as bounded typed fields.
The contracts are additive inside LedgerTargetCore, import no provider SDK, alter no Firebase target, open no hosted resource, and activate no production authority.
Later adapters may be replaced without changing the lifecycle semantics; removing this slice before cutover requires only reverting target-only code and evidence.

verification.expected: Canonical envelopes fingerprint deterministically; exact replay is idempotent; different payload reuse fails; and only reviewed lifecycle transitions succeed.
Encoding and restoring the journal preserves Account-scoped queued, applying, rejected, and resolved evidence and never upgrades local acceptance to server application.
Transient faults requeue, permanent rejection remains durable and recoverable, lost-response replay returns the prior result, different payload replay fails, and later unrelated operations continue.

Health validation rejects contradictory counts/timestamps, online and synchronized states remain distinct, required-update and migration blocks are explicit, and diagnostics contain no vendor message or payload.

notes: Decision-independent shared infrastructure. It deliberately stops before A-003/A-004 provider selection, A-015 optimistic projection mechanics, A-016 offline authorization lease, Supabase schema/handlers, PowerSync streams, app/MCP entry points, hosted resources, migration, or production authority.
